findings.claim: The DEM paper agent is told to update `INDEX.md` and `comparison_vs_ours.md`, but on the canonical branch those two files are the argyrodite-SE / DFT axis and explicitly exclude DEM·MPM digests. The correct targets are `INDEX_DEM.md` (auto-generated, hand-edits forbidden) and `comparison_vs_ours_DEM.md`. Following the agent file either pollutes the DFT track or blocks publication.
findings.evidence: File §5: "`INDEX.md`: set the paper's status → ✅ (edit the row)." and "`comparison_vs_ours.md`: add any new lit-vs-ours point under the right axis (A compaction/porosity / B transport triad / …)". Contradicted by canon `litdb/INDEX.md` header: "**이 파일은 SE(argyrodite) 축이다.** DEM·MPM·건식전극 digest 는 축이 달라 여기 없고 **`INDEX_DEM.md`** (자동 생성: `tools/litdb/build_index.py`) 에 있다"; by `litdb/INDEX_DEM.md` header: "이 파일은 `tools/litdb/build_index.py` 가 생성한다 — **손으로 고치지 말 것**"; and by `litdb/comparison_vs_ours.md` header: "DEM·MPM 논문은 축이 달라 여기 들어갈 자리가 없고 **`comparison_vs_ours_DEM.md`** 가 받는다. ⚠ 두 문서를 한 분모로 세면 … **가짜 미결**이 나온다." Measured on origin/claude/friendly-meitner-lldvar: the agent's own depth exemplar `bazzoun2026_dem_fem_rnm_ionic` appears 0× in INDEX.md and 1× in INDEX_DEM.md (same for kang2025_bollard…). Meanwhile `scripts/litdb_promote.py:228` gates only on `litdb/INDEX.md` ("✗ INDEX.md 에 등재 안 된 카드"), so a correctly-filed DEM card fails --close.
findings.proposed_action: Rewrite §5: DEM/MPM cards → row is produced by `python3 tools/litdb/build_index.py` (regenerate INDEX_DEM.md, never hand-edit); comparison point → `comparison_vs_ours_DEM.md` axes A–F; INDEX.md is off-limits for this agent. Separately file a note that `scripts/litdb_promote.py`'s --close INDEX gate must accept INDEX_DEM.md (or run build_index.py) or DEM cards cannot be published through the documented flow.

bucket_verdict: The `.claude` bucket is nine small, entirely live configuration/prompt files: one subagent definition, six wiki slash commands, one hook script and the settings file that wires it. Nothing here is dead or superseded, and nothing is a one-off analysis script — this is operational plumbing, and all of it is currently exercised (lint.py reports 21 pages / 0 errors, context_meter.py selftest 23/23, the hook exits 0, litdb_promote.py selftest passes). The wiki half (six commands + hook + settings) is healthy and self-consistent with wiki/SCHEMA.md, wiki/CLAUDE.md and root CLAUDE.md; its only weaknesses are organizational (wiki/queries/ has never been filed into, all 21 pages remain unverified, and /wiki-ingest routes paper publication at an unvalidated hand-rolled worktree recipe that duplicates scripts/litdb_promote.py). The litdb half is where the rot is: `.claude/agents/litdb-curator.md` was last touched 2026-07-28 and has since been overtaken by three separate canon moves — the canonical branch split its indexes and comparison documents by axis (INDEX_DEM.md, auto-generated, plus comparison_vs_ours_DEM.md) while the agent still writes to the argyrodite/DFT-axis files; CLAUDE.md's 2026-09-03 rule banned INDEX-based duplicate checking and explicitly told us to instruct agents to look at `papers/`, which this agent does not do (it has no dedup step at all); and CL-81 (2026-09-08) added a mandatory CONTACT_FREE caveat for exactly the literature-σ comparison this agent is built to write. It also contradicts itself on whether it may push. For a v3 reorganization: keep all nine files, but treat `.claude/` as a first-class norm surface rather than hidden config — the curator file needs a corrections pass (four P1s) and should be cross-linked from the litdb hub, and the wiki commands should be listed where CLAUDE.md names them so the operational entry points are discoverable without opening a dotfile directory. One out-of-bucket note picked up while checking the ban registry: `wiki/log.md:53` and `wiki/questions/sr01-delta-sigma-sign.md:69,79` carry the rounded form \"×35.8\" of the CL-15-banned \"×35.79\"; the pages do carry retraction banners, but the rounded variant is not in `quotation_ban`, so the sweep cannot see it — worth handing to whoever owns the wiki/ bucket.

bucket_verdict: The (root) bucket is the repo's public face plus a fossil layer beneath it: two config files that are quietly load-bearing, five root-level markdown docs of wildly different currency, and ten generated data/figure artefacts from a single 2026-05-13 porosity campaign. Only three items are unambiguously live — .gitattributes, .gitignore and STAGE_E_ASR_GUIDE.md. README.md is live but describes only the 2026-05/06 DEM+Stage-E paper pipeline and mentions neither the claims ledger, the mandatory `scripts/check_all.sh` gate, the discipline CI, the MPM/STEP kit, wiki/, nor the litdb canon branch; it is the single highest-value edit for a v3 hub. The two GB_correction docs form a supersession chain that was never marked: the n=21 comparison adopts an exponential fit (R^2 0.9614) and hands over a paste-ready manuscript sentence, while the n=41 v2.0 report one level away shows that same fit collapsing to R^2 0.0579 once thickness varies — and the v2.0 report in turn still presents v4++ FORM X (phi_c 0.18), a phi^(3/2) electronic law, and a compact thermal power law that CLAUDE.md has respectively demoted, exponent-locked at 4, and explicitly forbidden. Its generator has already been rewritten to emit the production forms, so the root copy is a snapshot masquerading as the live download. The ten porosity artefacts share one defect: the 2026-05-28 cut from 82 to 80 cases reached the two CSVs and stopped there, so every PNG, the 4-panel script's hard-coded panel counts, and the main.tex caption (N=82/33/20) still describe a corpus that includes two cases the project deleted as anomalies. bucket_verdict: This bucket is one file and it is fully alive: `.github/workflows/discipline.yml` is the repository's only CI configuration and the mechanical enforcer of the discipline regime CLAUDE.md describes. It is not a candidate for archiving under any reading — two production checkers parse it by literal path at runtime (`check_method_discipline.py`'s rule K via `K_CI_YML`, and `check_selftest_inventory.py` via `WORKFLOW`, which reads its `pip install` line to verify the CI dependency closure), so moving or renaming it in a v3 reorganization would break rule K and the inventory checker rather than merely orphan a reference. I verified it by execution rather than reading: all 26 script and test paths it invokes exist; the sealed LHS design file hashes to exactly the SHA256 pinned at line 109 (bc72b8bf...bd52ea19); and the three repo-real gates it runs all pass here (check_review_findings, check_method_discipline with rules A–O at 0 errors / 5 warnings, check_selftest_inventory --quiet). Its most load-bearing comment — that the inventory checker computes the dependency closure and will catch a missing entry in the pip line — is genuinely implemented (check_selftest_inventory.py:308-330, 366-368), not aspirational. One real gap: two repo-real gates that fire in `check_all.sh` do not fire in CI, the significant one being `check_cohort_packages.py`, which re-derives the committed evidence packages against the Table S3 ledger prose in 0.16 s; CI runs only its `--selftest`, which both CLAUDE.md and check_all.sh state does not substitute for the repo-real run. Two latent weaknesses worth carrying into v3 but not reportable as findings, since neither is currently misfiring: the quotation_ban sweep's `BAN_SCAN_GLOBS` (check_review_findings.py:104-129) covers CLAUDE.md, docs, wiki, webapp and deck generators but not `.github/**` or any `.yml`, so a retracted value written into a CI comment would not be swept — this file presently contains no banned values, only a SHA and step counts; and the inventory's `lanes()` helper matches script paths by string without checking the flag or excluding comment lines, so a script merely named in a comment would be credited as wired — I tested this against the workflow and all 26 credited names currently sit on real `run:` lines, so there is no active false-green today. For v3, this file should be surfaced at the front of the hub as the "what is actually enforced" entry point, not buried as infrastructure.

bucket_verdict: The bucket is a single file and it is unambiguously alive, not archivable. config/env_db.json is the machine-readable half of a deliberate two-source pair (docs/server_bootstrap_runbook.md is the prose twin, and the two agree), it is the sole data source for scripts/env_db.py, it is executed at the end of every server bootstrap, and its schema self-test runs in CI on every push — I ran it and it passes. Its physics-adjacent numbers (contrast-cap cost -7.8% / <=2.5 microvolt, CG iteration x5.2, GPU Jacobi 43.5 s vs AMG ladder 440.9 s = 10.1x, coarsest-at-114% guard) reproduce docs/step4_bottleneck_analysis_20260727.md exactly, and a sweep against all 22 claims.json quotation_ban patterns finds zero leaks — so it carries no retracted values. What is wrong with it is scope and freshness, in one recurring shape: the registry is complete only where a hand-written filter says to look. Its self-test compares knobs against a single file (scripts/step4_dyn.py) plus a three-name exemption tuple, so four live kit overrides that change D_s and i0 sit outside it; thirteen third-party imports sit outside the package list; host RAM, which is the constraint that actually stops the vox sweep, sits outside the machine profiles; and its own updated stamp still reads 2026-07-27 although a 2026-09-01 commit edited it. This is precisely the failure class CLAUDE.md discipline (5) names ("the code that picks the candidates is the blind spot") and that findings.json:1521 already recorded firing against this very file once. For v3: keep it, promote it to the hub front as the environment entry point (it answers a question nothing else in the repo answers), fix the four gaps above in one pass, and replace the hand list inside its self-test with a repo-wide sweep so the registry fails closed rather than after the next adversarial review. One P1 needs a decision outside this file: scripts/step6_surrogate.py:1024 advertises two kit env knobs (MPM_S4_RATE, MPM_S4_I0) that exist nowhere, and this DB is the evidence they were never real.

bucket_verdict: This bucket is two unrelated families plus one duplicate blob. The larger family, dem_scripts/oat_sweep/ (16 of the 22 files), is the healthiest thing here: a fully live, recently built (2026-08-25) run package whose 13 generated inputs I verified line by line against manifest.csv — 13/13 exact on types, E, both friction entries, COR and rolling friction, all sharing seed 78049, target_press 0.300 and volumefraction 0.281 — with a working generator (selftest 35/35, --check clean), a runner with real hard-won defensiveness in it, and a downstream analysis tool. It should be kept intact and surfaced in v3, not archived; its only defect is that its README froze on the day it was written and now contradicts the verdict doc that superseded it, and that it is the sole custodian of a still-open defect (heckel/*.liggghts non-executable, make_heckel_inputs.py still on .replace()) whose deferral condition cleared two weeks ago without the item ever reaching findings.json. The smaller family — the outlier seed-variance study (particulate12_seed.liggghts, the two runners, the zip) — is genuinely historical but not disposable: it is the provenance of corpus rows the canon still reasons about, so the inputs and run_all_outlier_seeds.sh should move to an archive that is indexed rather than deleted, while run_thin6_seeds.sh (fully subsumed) and outlier_seed_study.zip (byte-identical duplicate of five neighbours, referenced by nothing) can go. The two case09 E-sweep inputs are the awkward case: no results for either stiffness exist anywhere in the repo, so as a study they are historical, yet case09_E15x has been quietly promoted into the setup documentation as the canonical case to run — which is how v3 inherited both a factually wrong output claim (it writes LIGGGHTS dumps, not atoms.csv/contacts.csv, and the conversion step parse_liggghts.py is named in neither doc) and an unlabelled off-calibration example at 1.5x the production E_SE. Fixing the setup doc is the single highest-value action in this bucket; nothing here carries a quotation_ban leak or a model identifier.

bucket_verdict: Both files are alive, not dead one-offs. They are the seed-parameterized LIGGGHTS input decks for the 2026-05 outlier seed-variance study (thin_6 = 1 mAh 80:20 P:S 7:3; thin_9 = 1 mAh 85:15 P:S 7:3), and they are the reproduction source for ten cases still in the production corpus (input_1mAh_6_S1..S5, input_1mAh_9_S1..S4, verified present in all_dem_porosity.csv and docs/data/case_master.csv with compositions matching the decks). Beyond provenance they now serve a second, load-bearing role: docs/reviews/claims.json:1634 cites thin6 as the authority for the phase<->atom-type mapping and the simulation unit scale, and docs/temp_pressure_capability.md:54 cites thin9 as the pipeline's compaction-pressure knob. I checked the content against canon and found nothing scientifically wrong: the mass-fraction PDD reading is the one scripts/dem_input_values.py:149 confirmed by particle-count measurement (0.07 % error), the pressure-triggered displacement stop plus relax matches CLAUDE.md's own \"hold = LIGGGHTS displacement-stop+relax\" characterization and the 2026-08-30 oat resolution, the platen speed is far inside the quasi-static band, and a mechanical sweep of all 22 quotation_ban strings in claims.json against both files returned zero hits. What is wrong is packaging: neither deck states its unit scale, even though the repo has a written convention for exactly that (`Scale: r×1000, E×0.001, P×0.001`) which the current-standard 6 mAh Phase A deck docs/data/phase_a_6mah/in.real_4.liggghts does carry - and canon points readers at thin9 line 18 to edit the pressure, which is where that omission turns into a wrong-experiment hazard (P1). The deck -> corpus-case rename (thin_N -> 1mAh_N) is documented nowhere, one runner will silently regenerate a case CLAUDE.md records as deleted, a byte-identical unreferenced zip duplicates both files, and a header names a format that exists nowhere. For v3: keep both decks, move them under a documented STEP1 / DEM-inputs section with a small README carrying the deck -> case-family map and the unit-scale block, retire dem_scripts/outlier_seed_study.zip and the subset runner run_thin6_seeds.sh, and add the DEM input-deck layer to the wiki (it currently has zero mentions of dem_scripts, starting its DEM pipeline page at the dumps).

bucket_verdict: This bucket is not code and nothing in it is dead: all 22 files are immutable primary literature — 19 PDFs, 2 SI .docx files, 1 SI .pdf, and 1 text extraction — and every one of them is live evidence behind something the repo still leans on. Sixteen have a dedicated litdb digest card (176-596 lines each) plus, in fourteen cases, a machine-readable docs/data/*_anchors.csv; the remaining six are supporting-information files reachable only through a "(+ `_SI.docx`)" / "(+ `_SI.pdf`)" suffix in their main paper's card header, which is exactly why a basename grep reports five of them as unreferenced and why a topic-driven audit reached none of the 22. Nothing here should be archived. The real problem is findability at two levels. First, the directory's own README declares itself the single source of truth for docs/literature_coverage/ but its "## Files" section lists only two files and never mentions pdfs/ at all — the index of record is actually litdb/INDEX.md, one directory over, and nothing says so. Second, the suffix-shorthand convention for SI files hides primary sources: the sharpest instance is that CL-81, the newest canon entry (2026-09-08), holds an open item asking someone to verify R_i,gb / R_i,bulk against the primary source and states the values exist only as a docstring citation — while docs/data/kim2025_tlm_kinetics_anchors.csv carries them tagged stated,S3 and Kim_2025_..._SI.docx in this very bucket contains Table S3 verbatim. That is CLAUDE.md rule ⑤'s subset-filter false-green, reproduced on a documentation lookup. For v3: keep the whole directory, give it a real index (author, year, journal, slug, card path, anchor CSV) that lists SI files as first-class rows rather than suffixes, rename the two author-less files before they cause a second mis-citation of the kind CLAUDE.md already had to correct on 2026-08-19, and back-annotate the two cards whose guidance canon has since overruled (Kang E=175) or already satisfied (kim2025 Table S3).

This bucket is three unrelated families and almost nothing in it is dead. (1) Fourteen literature PDFs plus two SI files in docs/literature_coverage/pdfs/ — every single one has a matching litdb/papers/ digest card, so they are live source data and should move as a unit under whatever v3 calls the literature store; do not archive any of them. (2) Three CSVs — docs/case_summary.csv and docs/full_ranking.csv are live (four scripts read the first, rank_all_cases writes the second, and both are already inventoried in docs/data_inventory_20260825.md and consistent with CLAUDE.md's record of the 2026-05-28 sibling-tail deletion, verified by checking that 1mAh_9_S5 and particulate_12_S2 are indeed absent), and docs/db/section7_10case_sweep.csv is the live data anchor for manuscript Section 7. (3) Three JSON knowledge bases in docs/literature_coverage/ that split cleanly: contact_mechanics_db.json is current and genuinely useful and should be surfaced; coverage_db.json's literature entries are fine but its k_spread-calibration framing is superseded by the parameter-free physics-mode coverage convention; packing_regime_db.json's physics blocks hold but its scaling_law_evolution log and session roadmap are an April-2026 fossil that still reads as live instructions to add sigma_ionic form terms and re-fit phi_c, which CLAUDE.md's T1 section explicitly forbids — that block needs a HISTORICAL stamp in v3, not deletion (it is the record of a real dead end). The one thing that needs fixing rather than reorganizing is the thermal unit: the sigma_th column of section7_10case_sweep.csv is correctly labelled mS/cm in the CSV but is reproduced in the manuscript's Table 7.1 as W/mK with no conversion, and grade_engine turns the same mS/cm-scale quantity into an 'ASR_thermal (K·cm²/W)' axis with absolute thresholds that scores into docs/full_ranking.csv — both on top of values that per the live ledger entry CL-12 were computed with the thermal weighting branch dead and have never been re-measured since the 2026-08-12 fix. CONTRADICTING SOURCE scripts/grade_engine.py:500-505: "'key': '__asr_thermal_Kcm2_W', 'label': 'ASR_thermal (K·cm²/W)', 'direction': 'lower', 'thresholds': [1.5, 2.5, 4, 6, 9, 14], 'formula': 'ASR_th = L_cathode × 0.1 / κ'"; :948-952 computes it as 'float(L) * 0.1 / float(k)' where k = _kappa_effective(metrics) -> 'thermal_sigma_full_mScm_stage_e_physics' (:753-757). The IDENTICAL expression 'float(L) * 0.1 / float(s)' is used 8 lines earlier at :940-945 for '__asr_electronic_Ohm_cm2', which yields Ω·cm² from mS/cm — i.e. the same arithmetic on a mS/cm-scale number is relabelled K·cm²/W. CLAUDE.md §σ_thermal Stage T1 states the solver scale is 'Kirchhoff-normalized solver mScm-equiv' that literature W/m·K values 'don't map to', and network_conductivity.py:327-340 shows the thermal weights are dimensionless ratios on the ionic baseline.
findings.proposed_action: Either drop the K·cm²/W label and the absolute thresholds on the ASR_thermal axis (report it as a relative thermal-resistance proxy, rank-only), or establish a real absolute scale by feeding the solver k_AM/k_SE in W/(m·K) instead of a relative weight on sigma_SE. Until then the axis (weight 0.15) should not be presented in the served grade-guide as an engineering K·cm²/W number.
